text:
Artemi Panarin is 35 and in his first full season in Los Angeles, after the Rangers moved him to the Kings, and he still plays like the most dangerous man on the ice. He has 20 points in 18 games, half on the power play, and the Kings take 60% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on at five on five, 15 points better than without him.

If anything he's been unlucky. His teammates have scored 9.0 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him out there, which has cost him points; that kind of gap usually swings back. His own shooting, 14%, sits right where our talent range says it should.

He missed time in mid-November for family reasons, per Daily Faceoff, and returned against Montreal on Nov. 23. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking still had him 91st percentile in shot assists last season, carrying the puck in on 55% of his entries. Watch the assists: the chances he's creating are running ahead of what his linemates have finished.
headline: Panarin is creating more than LA is finishing
